tired-of-politics.name: Tired of politics
tired-of-politics.line: Thinking about politics leaves me worn out and angry.

sources.passage: nearly two-thirds of Americans (65%) say they always or often feel exhausted when thinking about politics, while 55% feel angry. By contrast, just 10% say they always or often feel hopeful about politics

tired-of-politics.prevalence: 65% of U.S. adults always or often feel exhausted thinking about politics, 55% feel angry, and just 10% feel hopeful (Pew Research Center survey).

no-time-to-help.name: Time to volunteer
no-time-to-help.line: I'd like to get involved, but work and family leave me no time.

sources.passage: the most common barriers to participating in formal volunteering were:: ‘I have work commitments’ – 51% ‘I do other things in my spare time’ – 32% ‘I have to look after children’ – 22%

no-time-to-help.prevalence: In England, 51% of adults who did not volunteer monthly named work commitments as a barrier and 22% named looking after children (Community Life Survey).

organizer-burnout.name: Organizer burnout
organizer-burnout.line: I've worked for change so long that I'm running on empty.

sources.passage: The poll found that burnout, low pay, and institutional barriers to seizing power make up a trifecta of issues facing organizers at all time scales.
only 32 percent believed they’d still be organizing in five years
surveyed 349 organizers from across the country

organizer-burnout.prevalence: In a re:power poll of 349 U.S. organizers, burnout was a top concern and only 32 percent expected to still be organizing in five years.

threats-for-serving.name: Harassed for serving
threats-for-serving.line: I see people who serve on local boards and councils get threatened and harassed.

sources.passage: The numbers balloon to 89 percent of state legislators and 52 percent of local officeholders when less severe forms of abuse — insults or harassment such as stalking — are included.
More than 40 percent of local officeholders said they were less willing to run for reelection or higher office at the time they were surveyed because of abuse.

threats-for-serving.prevalence: 52 percent of U.S. local officeholders faced threats, attacks, insults or harassment, and more than 40 percent were less willing to run again because of abuse (Brennan Center).
